prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Golf kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Golf
- the CAP face up with its brim towards the viewer, the BELT laid out straight, and the SINGLE GLOVE laid palm down — ONE glove only, never a pair — each its own separate item, never on top of another garment

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: An OLIVE short-sleeved golf POLO exactly as photo2.png shows it: plain olive all over including the COLLAR and the sleeves — the collar is the SAME olive as the body and is NOT a contrasting colour, whatever the sport default says. A normal fold-over polo collar and a short placket with THREE buttons, all olive. The club badge sits HIGH ON THE LEFT CHEST just below the collar: the pinewick-osprey mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — an INVERTED clipped TRIANGLE, two corners at the top and the point at the bottom, with an OFF-WHITE field inside an olive border and the osprey seen head-on inside it, wings raised into a wide V and talons reaching down. It is the ONLY mark on the polo. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering of any kind. The BACK of the polo is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN OLIVE: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Golf does not number a shirt, and a number across her back would be a mark this polo does not have.
- shorts: OLIVE TAILORED GOLF TROUSERS exactly as photo2.png shows them — full length to the shoe, a straight slim leg with a pressed front crease, a flat waistband with BELT LOOPS but NO BELT worn through them, and slash pockets at the hips. Plain olive, no stripe, no logo, no lettering. photo3.png shows her practising in olive SHORTS on a warm day; those are training wear, and the DECISION for every pose is the TROUSERS from photo2.png, which are the on-course kit.
- socks: PLAIN WHITE ANKLE SOCKS, sitting just above the shoe collar, no stripe and no maker's mark, as photo3.png shows them. In photo2.png the trousers cover them entirely, which is correct — with the trousers on, little or no sock shows.
- footwear: PLAIN WHITE GOLF SHOES exactly as photo3.png shows them: a low white leather-look shoe with white laces, a slightly rounded toe and a flat spikeless outsole. Completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED — no stripes device, no swoosh, no maker's mark and no lettering on the upper or the sole. This is her GOLF footwear and it appears in the golf frames — photo2.png and photo3.png. photo1.png is a day at home and she is in ordinary plain grey trainers there, which are not kit and are not this pair. They are WORN IN rather than new: photo1.png and photo3.png both show grass stain and dried mud across the toe and the outsole from playing, which is correct for shoes that live on a course, and photo2.png does not show her feet at all. In the poses they read as a real pair she plays in — lightly marked, never factory-fresh and never filthy.
- equipment: THREE THINGS, and all three are hers. A GOLF CLUB with a plain polished silver steel shaft and a plain black grip, completely unbranded — no maker's name on the head, the shaft or the grip. A single GLOVE worn on her LEFT hand — her leading hand, she plays right-handed — in soft pale leather with a small round ball marker on the closure — it reads olive-grey in photo2.png and closer to white in photo3.png, and the DECISION for the poses is the PALE OLIVE-GREY of photo2.png, the frame that shows her match kit; ONE glove only, never a pair, and the right hand is bare. And an OLIVE CAP with a curved brim, plain and unmarked, with the ponytail threaded out behind it. In photo2.png she is also carrying a plain unbranded golf BAG of clubs and a CLEAR plastic water bottle with a blue cap and NO label on it at all, on her way round; a second bottle stands on the grass behind her with a plain unreadable wrap; the DECISION for the poses is that she carries the CLUB and nothing else — no bag, no bottle, no towel, and no ball unless the action needs one, in which case it is a plain white unbranded ball.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits HIGH ON THE LEFT CHEST just below the collar, about three fingers wide, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits HIGH ON THE LEFT CHEST just below the collar, about three fingers wide, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
